newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain electric protocol to be signed Wed or Thurs.
newsitem.headline: Spain electric protocol to be signed Wed or Thurs.

text.p: Spanish electricity firms and the Industry Ministry are due to sign a protocol for a new set of regulations governing the sector this week, likely on Wednesday, a spokesman for the Industry Ministry said on Monday.
"The protocol should be signed on Wednesday, or if not, Thursday," the spokesman told Reuters.
The document will set out an agreed framework under which the liberalisation of the electricity sector can take place, the aim being to open it up to foreign companies from 1998.
The new framework will include an estimation of overall sunk costs of 1.9 trillion pesetas, the spokesman said.
Sunk or stranded costs, broadly defined as fixed costs which under the current regime are subsidised via electricity tariffs, includes subsidies for the use of national coal, he said.
But electricity companies will be given more time to determine amongst themselves how stranded costs will be split, the spokesman said.
The companies will be allowed to pass on these costs via tariffs in the next 10 years, Industry Minister Josep Pique said on Saturday.
He also confirmed that electricity rates will fall eight percent on average in the next five years under the new protocol.
